newsitem.title: USA: Danskin says in $10 mln investment pact.
newsitem.headline: Danskin says in $10 mln investment pact.

text.p: Danskin Inc said Tuesday that an investment firm has reached an agreement in which Danskin Investors LLC will make a $10 million equity investment in the company.

In the proposed deal, Danskin Investors, a newly-formed firm, will buy common shares of the activewear maker at $0.38 a share, it said. The investor is a firm formed by a group led by Onyx Partners Inc, it said.
Donald Schupak, Danskin's chairman, said that under its present loan agreement with its principal lender it is required to raise at least $6.0 million by the end of August.

"Consummation of the agreement with the investor will satisfy this requirement, and will create a meaningful reduction in debt with a corresponding increase in working capital, coupled with a reasonable opportunity, under the circumstances, for current equity to participate in the future of Danskin," he said.

Danskin said the transaction is subject to certain conditions, including the negotiation of a definitive stock purchase agreement and the conclusion of certain agreements with the company's principal bank lender and other parties, it said.
Danskin said it and the investor will seek to negotiate a restructuring of its debt and intends to review its loan and security agreement with its principal lender as soon as possible.

If an agreement were reached the lender, the investor could buy up to $4.0 million in a new series of Danskin convertible preferred stock. The stock would be convertible into Danskin common stock at $0.38 a share, it said.
The transaction would require Danskin stockholder approvel to raise the company's authorized common shares, it said.

If the transaction were completed, Danskin added, its agreement with the investor also calls for it to offer to all Danskin stockholders, on a pro-rata basis, rights to subscribe to 3.0 million common shares at $0.38 a share.
It said the investor has agreed to be a standby purchaser of any shares in the offer not bought by shareholders.
